prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: modular hand-tool source board for a classic painted 2D strategy game
Input images: Images 1 and 2 are exact layout, component scale, rendering-quality, lighting, and chroma-key references only.
Primary request: Create one practical frontier hand spade in four genuine orthographic views. It has a straight weathered ash-wood handle, a small dark forged-iron D grip at the top, a narrow reinforced neck, and a compact pointed iron digging blade at the bottom. It should read immediately as a civilian digging spade, not a weapon or oversized shovel.
Scene/backdrop: perfectly flat uniform solid #ff00ff chroma-key background.
Style/medium: match the references' high-quality painted raster game-component style, crisp dark contour clusters, controlled warm highlights, visible wood grain and hammered iron, consistent three-quarter game lighting.
Composition/framing: exact 1536x1024 landscape board. Four isolated vertical tools arranged left to right: front view, back view, left-edge/profile view, right-edge/profile view. In every view the D grip is at the top and pointed blade at the bottom. Keep each complete, uncropped, non-overlapping, centered in its own quarter, with generous magenta padding.
Tool invariants: identical handle length, D grip, neck band, blade shape, material colors, and wear in every view; profile views must show the blade thickness and slight forward dish rather than being duplicate flat fronts.
Constraints: tool only; no hands, person, dirt, plants, extra parts, shadow, floor, texture, gradient, border, labels, text, or watermark. Background must be one exact flat color with no lighting variation. Do not use #ff00ff within the tool. Crisp silhouette.
Avoid: spear, polearm, axe, hoe, broad modern shovel, ornate fantasy weapon, rust flakes detached from the blade, merged tools, floating fragments, photoreal product photo, soft airbrushed edges.
